provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — inbound documents with remote-template references / equation-editor objects and region-specific government/port lures are detectable at the mail gateway and sandbox via attachment inspection, template-injection detection and sender/lure analytics
medium — links/LNK-in-ZIP are detectable at the mail gateway and via detonation, but geofenced servers frequently withhold the payload from sandboxes, limiting verdicts
medium — Office spawning child processes (e.g. EQNEDT32.EXE, mshta.exe) after a user opens a document is detectable via process-lineage telemetry, but the open action itself is user-driven
medium — LNK execution spawning mshta.exe with a remote URL is detectable via process-creation command-line telemetry

high — EQNEDT32.EXE spawning mshta.exe / making outbound network connections is a well-known, high-fidelity exploit signature detectable via process-lineage and EDR; the Equation Editor should not launch children
high — mshta.exe launched with a remote URL, spawned by Office/EQNEDT32/LNK, and making outbound HTTP requests is a strong, actor-relevant detection via process command-line and network telemetry

medium — script-heavy execution under mshta and manipulation of the COMPLUS_Version environment variable are detectable via command-line/environment and script-block telemetry, but obfuscation limits static verdicts
medium — DDE-driven child processes from Office are detectable via process-lineage, though this vector is largely superseded by the CVE-2017-11882 equation-editor chain in recent MENA activity
medium — in-memory .NET assembly loading is detectable via CLR/AMSI and memory-scan telemetry, but is stealthier than file-based execution and needs runtime instrumentation

high — a signed application loading an unsigned/anomalous DLL by these names from an unusual path is detectable via module-load (Sysmon EID 7) and signature/path-mismatch telemetry; frequent name rotation argues for behavioral (load-location) rather than name-only rules

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation/modification of Run-key autostart entries pointing to the loader/host binary is detectable via registry-modification telemetry (Sysmon EID 13) and autoruns baselining
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) and detectable when it launches the loader/host binary from an unusual path
medium — registry writes to autostart and config locations are detectable via registry-modification telemetry, but blend with legitimate software installs without baselining

detection_candidates.technique_name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
detection_candidates.rationale: high — common UAC-bypass primitives (auto-elevating COM/fodhelper/eventvwr-style hijacks) are detectable via registry-hijack and anomalous elevated-process-lineage telemetry
medium — sandbox-check logic is visible on sample analysis but leaves little live host signal; primarily a hunt/sample-analysis indicator

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy/obfuscated script content and control-flow-flattened assemblies are detectable via entropy/heuristic and script-block analytics but generate analyst overhead

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy encrypted blobs and Base64 payloads are detectable via file-entropy analytics but require dedicated scanning

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — legitimately-named DLLs in unexpected paths and signature-vs-name mismatches are detectable via path/hash baselining, but name rotation reduces static-signature value

high — WMI queries against SecurityCenter2 / AntiVirusProduct and rapid enumeration of many security-product process names are detectable via WMI-activity and process-access telemetry, and are characteristic of this chain
medium — bulk process enumeration is common but suspicious when tightly correlated with the mshta/.NET-loader lineage
medium — system-info collection is routine and noisy; meaningful mainly within the loader process-lineage window
medium — network-config discovery commands (ipconfig, route) are detectable via command-line telemetry but common; value from recon-burst correlation
medium — whoami / user-context queries are detectable in command-line logs but common; meaningful in recon-burst context
medium — file/directory enumeration is common and noisy; meaningful mainly within a tight process-lineage window
medium — software/framework enumeration is detectable via registry-read and WMI telemetry but blends with legitimate activity
medium — screen capture leaves little discrete signal; detectable mainly via API-behavior heuristics in EDR and correlation with the implant process
medium — keylogging is detectable via low-level keyboard-hook API behavior in EDR but is not always distinctive without implant correlation
medium — automated bulk file access/staging is detectable via file-access and process I/O telemetry, but needs baselining to separate from legitimate use
medium — local data collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging patterns and implant process-lineage
medium — creation of local staging files/directories preceding egress is detectable via file-write telemetry with baselining

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: high — access to browser credential stores (Login Data SQLite, DPAPI decryption) is detectable via file-access and process-behavior telemetry in EDR
high — access to lsass.exe memory for Windows credential theft is highly observable via EDR process-access telemetry
medium — spoofed credential-prompt GUIs are hard to detect directly; observable via anomalous process spawning a credential dialog and correlation with the implant
high — outbound HTTP/HTTPS to the enumerated C2/look-alike domains is detectable via proxy/DNS telemetry and domain bl:ocklisting; DNS/proxy logs are the primary network detection surface
high — remote payload retrieval by mshta.exe and the .NET loader, and file writes following those downloads, are detectable via network + process/file telemetry
medium — encrypted C2 defeats payload inspection; detectable via JA3/JA4 TLS fingerprinting, beacon-timing analytics and destination reputation rather than content

medium — implant-provided reverse shells are detectable via anomalous outbound connections and interactive-command process-lineage from the implant, but there is no third-party RMM binary to signature
medium — exfiltration over the C2 channel is detectable via outbound-volume anomalies and destination reputation, though encryption hides content
medium — periodic automated egress is detectable via beacon-plus-transfer timing analytics, but blends with normal encrypted traffic without baselining

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — reconnaissance/targeting messaging is largely off-victim and observable only at the email gateway when links are present; hunt candidate via mail-gateway URL and lure-theme analytics
low — malware development happens off-victim on adversary infrastructure; intel/hunt candidate tracked via sample clustering and family evolution
low — domain registration is off-victim; hunt/intel candidate via newly-registered-domain and brand-impersonation monitoring for organization/port names
low — geofenced/off-victim staging defeats sandbox retrieval and is not endpoint-observable; hunt/intel candidate via infrastructure tracking and retrieval from in-region sensors
low — evasion designed to defeat automated analysis leaves minimal host telemetry; hunt/intel candidate via in-region detonation and infrastructure analysis
low — in-memory decode/decrypt routines leave little discrete host signal; primarily a sample-analysis characteristic
low — system-time queries are ubiquitous and low-signal; not a practical standalone detection
